source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 3, 49. Ἀντὶ τοῦ ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου κατεπονήθη, καὶ οὐ σιγήσε- ται τοῦ μὴ εἶναι ἔκνηψιν Σύμμαχος εἶπεν· ὸ ὀφθαλμός μου ἐπέμεινε, καὶ οὐκ ἐπαύσατο τοῦ μὴ εἶναι ἄνεσιν. δηλοῦσι δὲ οἱ μὲν Ἑβδομήκοντα ὅτι καίπερ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ἐκ πλήθους δακρύων ἠσθενηκότων οὐ διέλειπον ὅμως, ἀνανῆψαι τοῦ κλαυθμοῦ μὴ δυνά- μενος, ὁ δὲ Σύμμαχος ὅτι ἐπέμεινά τε δακρύων καὶ οὐ διέλειπον· προσευχὴ γὰρ ἐκτενὴς καὶ δακρύων ἐπίτασις τὸν θεὸν ἐφέλκει πρὸς ἔλεον.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] Instead of “my eye was worn out, and it will not be silent from there being no sobering,” Symmachus said: “my eye persisted, and it did not cease from there being no relief.” And the Seventy show that although the eyes had weakened from a multitude of tears they still were not leaving off—he not being able to sober from the weeping—and Symmachus that I both persisted weeping and was not leaving off; for stretched-out prayer and intensification of tears draws God toward mercy.
pass_b_english: Instead of “my eye was worn out, and it will not be silent from there being no sobering,” (Lamentations 3:49) Symmachus said: “my eye persisted, and it did not cease from there being no relief.” And the Seventy show that although the eyes had weakened from a multitude of tears they still were not leaving off—he not being able to sober from the weeping—and Symmachus that I both persisted weeping and was not leaving off; for stretched-out prayer and intensification of tears draws God toward mercy.

choices.why: Pauline echo at Lam 3:48 in Origen’s reading.
